do: Use short, punchy declaratives and fragments
Address the reader as 'you' and make it personal ('your tools, your way')
Lead with the feeling or outcome, not the feature list
Use dry wit sparingly to signal self-awareness
Ground claims in specifics (crash-free rate, extension count)
dont: Write long explanatory paragraphs or feature-dump prose
Use passive voice or corporate hedging language
Over-explain what a keyboard launcher is
Use exclamation-point hype or breathless enthusiasm
Invent emotional narratives — let the product speak through concrete outcomes
